newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to watch - Aug 12.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS - Issues to watch - Aug 12.

text.p: -- Some Wall Street investors are wondering whether Coca-Cola Co's earnings warning Friday will take momentum out of the broader stock market, the Wall Street Journal reported in its "Heard on the Street" column. Coca-Cola said Friday its third quarter earnings would only "slightly exceed" year-earlier results. Coke closed Monday at 61-3/4 and has been the most actively traded stock on the New York Stock Exchange, falling 5.8 percent Friday and a further 1.5 percent Monday.

-- Two of the largest commercial banks in the Southeaset, First Union and Barnett Banks -- are among the likely bidders for Quick & Reilly Group which put itself up for sale Monday, the New York Times reported, citing investment bankers. The bids were likely to value the company at about $1.3 billion or 16 times its annual earnings, the report said. A report in the Wall Street Journal said Quick & Reilly had hired an investment bank to look for a buyer and that the brokerage could fetch as much as $1.5 billion. Quick & Reilly closed at 29-5/16, First Union closed at 47-9/16, and Barnett Banks closed at 54-5/16.

-- J.C. Penney Co Inc said late Monday it will offer voluntary early retirement to about 1,500 people, or 5 percent of its management staff, in a bid to cut costs to compensate for recent weak profits. Penney closed Monday at 58-1/8, up 0-1/2.

-- Cephalon Inc and Chiron Corp said Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has extended its review period for the new drug application submitted for clearance to market Myotrophin. The review has been extended to November 11 for the drug used to treat Lou Gehrig's disease. Cephalon closed at 12-2/16, and Chiron closed at 20-6/32.
